{{nihongo|'''Yatagarasu Shrine'''|八咫烏神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Uda, Nara|Q863747|qid=Q863747}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=small Shikinaisha}} listed in the '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}'. Its former rank was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. {{nihongo|'''Yatagarasu Shrine'''|八咫烏神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

== Enshrined deity ==
It enshrines {{ill|Kamotaketsunumi no Mikoto|it|Kamotaketsunumi no Mikoto|ja|賀茂建角身命|zh|賀茂建角身命|qid=Q11634939|lt=Taketsunumi-no-Mikoto}} ({{ill|Yatagarasu|ar|ياتاغاراسو|bcl|Yatagarasu|br|Yatagarasu|cs|Jatagarasu|de|Yatagarasu|es|Yatagarasu|fa|یاتاگاراسو|fr|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏|ko|야타가라스|la|Yatagarasu|no|Yatagarasu|pl|Yatagarasu|ru|Ятагарасу|simple|Yatagarasu|uk|Ятаґарасу|zh|八咫烏|qid=Q745463}}).

== History ==
In the '{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}', in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|Q357246|qid=Q357246}}, there is an entry that in {{ill|Keiun|Q428753|qid=Q428753}} 2 ({{ill|705|Q23504|qid=Q23504}}), Yatagarasu-sha was worshiped, and this is taken as the founding of this shrine<ref>Entry for day bōjutsu (9th) in 9th month.</ref>. In documentary terms, it is the first shrine in Japan to worship Yatagarasu as a deity.

Also, according to the 'Shinsen Shōjiroku,' when {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}} moved east to Yamato, Taketsunumi-no-Mikoto transformed into "Yatagarasu" and guided the stalled imperial party through the mountains of {{ill|Kumano region|Q6443450|qid=Q6443450}} to Yamato, contributing to imperial victory.

Because of this history, it was revered since ancient times as a {{ill|Military god|Q11637440|qid=Q11637440}}, and in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, the shrine is said to have greatly prospered under deep devotion of {{ill|Emperor Go-Daigo|Q313942|qid=Q313942}}<ref>"Brief Origin of Yatagarasu Shrine," Bunsei 13 year of Kanoe-Tora, Ōe no Toshitsune.</ref>.

However, after decline of the {{ill|Southern Court|Q3001082|qid=Q3001082|lt=Southern Court}} and repeated war damage, it fell near abolition until the mid-{{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, and it is said "yatagarasu" became colloquially slurred to "otogorosu"<ref>Hayashi Sōho, 'Washū Kyūseki Yūkō,' Enpō 9.</ref>.

Later, in {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} years of the Edo period, priests of {{ill|Shimogamo Shrine|Q701620|qid=Q701620}} (Shimogamo-sha) in {{ill|Kyōto|Q740246|qid=Q740246}} took notice, and through their efforts and cooperation of local volunteers, revival was achieved. It is said the honden was rebuilt into current {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|es|Kasuga-zukuri|fr|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造|ru|Касуга-дзукури|qid=Q3193781}} style around this time (the stone small shrine of the former honden still remains beside the honden).

After that, for annual grand festivals, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=heihaku envoys}} were sent from Shimogamo-sha and rites held, but because such grand rites with envoys were too heavy a burden for local parishioners then numbering only about nine households, and due guidance from Nara prefectural authorities concerned the shrine might be treated as an outside-precinct massha of Shimogamo-sha, Shimogamo participation was discontinued in early Meiji<ref>"Uda District Historical Materials."</ref>.

Later, in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 3 ({{ill|1917|Q2092|qid=Q2092}}), due to the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shrine Merger Ordinance}}, nearby guardian shrines came to be worshiped here, causing sudden revival.

In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}, related to {{ill|2600th Anniversary Celebrations of the Japanese Empire|Q5366450|qid=Q5366450}}, it was promoted to kensha, and precinct expansion and improvement were carried out. It has continued to the present.
